changelog.change: Added poolDir and poolPerBand, the Infinite Mode's pre-generated pool.
changelog.why: Row 22 - there is no runtime generator (Holy Law #1), so an endless Mode has to have every board it can ever deal baked in advance, and these two knobs are where that pool lands and how deep it goes. poolDir sits beside bankDir and under frontend/public/ for the same reason the bank does: the game reads it same-origin from its own bundle. poolPerBand is 100 and the number was measured rather than picked. It is a CEILING per Game per difficulty band, so 100 buys 300 boards a Game and 1,765 in total - the word-ladder's hard band stops at 65 because the reachability graph only holds that many four-rung climbs it has not already used, which is the ceiling behaving correctly rather than a shortfall to pad. The cost is 1,371,555 bytes of item files plus about 70,000 of index, and it is the largest single addition of bytes in the repo, so here is the arithmetic that made it acceptable: a pool is never fetched in bulk, a player downloads one index of roughly 12,000 bytes to start a stream and then 387 to 1,565 bytes a board, so the whole pool costs a phone nothing it does not play. What 100 buys the player is the anti-repeat promise actually meaning something: the Mode's LRU window is 200 picks, and a stream rotating the six Games at one difficulty draws from 565 distinct boards, nearly three times the window, so a repeat inside it is impossible rather than merely unlikely - and even a player who pins one Game and one band meets 100 boards, well over an hour, before the oldest-first recycle begins. Two alternatives were measured and rejected. Sixty per band would have cost 830,000 bytes and left a single-band stream of 339 boards, still above the window but with no headroom for a Game whose bucket runs out. Pricing each Game by BYTES rather than by boards - which would give the wordle three times the depth of the word search, since a search grid renders at 1,565 bytes against 387 - was rejected because equal depth per Game is a property the player can feel and equal bytes is not.

changelog.change: Registered the word-ladder generator: a climb of three or four rungs from a 2 to 4 ezhuthu start, picked from a bank of eight, with no attempt budget and no hint ladder.
changelog.why: Row 16 - the sixth Game, and the second whose difficulty dial is how many answers the board asks for rather than how long they are. targets is the rung count and it is the only dial that can be one here, because what makes a climb hard is the number of steps and how familiar the words along it are, not the width of the first one: measured over the served set, a shorter start is EASIER rather than harder, since three quarters of the two-ezhuthu multisets have a word one letter above them (1,384 of 1,812) against under a tenth of the five-ezhuthu ones (659 of 9,020) and none at all of the seven-ezhuthu ones. The bands therefore all start at 2 ezhuthu and separate on familiarity and rung count - easy is 3 rungs from the most familiar quarter, medium 3 rungs from the top half, hard 4 rungs from anywhere - and the ceiling stops at 4 because the graph does: of 35,991 ezhuthu multisets only 6,563 can be climbed from at all, 2,052 can carry three rungs and 623 four, so a five-rung band would have 154 starts in the whole language. What that leaves is still years of content: 994 of the 3,009 rows the easy band claims can be climbed three rungs, 632 of medium's 7,150, and 87 of hard's 7,525. attempts is 1 and is UNREAD, on the search board's terms - a ladder is a chain, so ending it mid-way would confiscate the rungs already earned, and a wrong pick therefore costs time rather than a life. hints is empty and that is a ruling rather than an omission: every rung the shared ladder can render is a fact about ONE word, and on this board that word is always the NEXT one, so the rung would have to be bought at the only moment it is worth anything and would then hand over most of a word three or four letters long. The help this Game gives instead is a per-rung reveal priced in the rung it hands over, which is a play-time fact and lives in the Game - so config/app-config.json needs no hints.perGame entry and the allowance reads as zero. choiceCount is 8, the missing-letters number, and it is the same bet: there is no Tamil keyboard, so the bank is how an addition is entered at all, and eight puts a player who knows nothing at one in eight a rung. dailyRank is 25, between the missing-letters board and the wordle: a climb is two or three bank picks in a chain, which is heavier than one bank pick and lighter than the only board a player can lose.

changelog.change: Gave every Game a dailyRank, and registered themed-nature under the missing-letters board as well as the anagram.
changelog.why: The Daily now holds three different Games a day, so something has to say which of them the player meets first, and dailyRank is that statement. A day deals its slots the difficulty bands in order and fills them with its Games in ascending rank, so both dials rise together and the day opens on the lightest board at its easiest band and closes on the heaviest at its hardest - which is what 'a day opens easy and ends harder' has to mean once a day is no longer three of the same Game. The numbers are a design order rather than a derived one, because what makes a board heavy is how many answers it asks for AND whether the player can lose it, and no single column says both: 10 the anagram, one word with every one of its ezhuthu already on the screen and a three-rung ladder, the fastest win in the game and therefore the day's opener; 20 the missing-letters board, one word with most of it printed but an ezhuthu to produce from a bank of eight rather than tiles to rearrange; 30 the wordle, one word from nothing and the only board a player can spend eight guesses on and still lose, so it is never an opener; 40 the search grid, four to six answers - the first board that asks for more than one thing - though none of them can be lost; 50 the crossword, four to six answers that constrain each other, each behind a clue that has to be read, the heaviest board in the game and the one a day should end on. Registering the theme under the missing-letters board is what lets a themed day hold more than one Game, and it was chosen by measurement rather than by symmetry: over themed-nature's 429 rows the anagram and this board together fill 62 consecutive themed dates without repeating a word, against 58 for the anagram alone, because two Games spread the draw across two sets of difficulty buckets instead of exhausting one. The other three stay unregistered for reasons that are equally measured and are the whole argument for a separate themed ring - the wordle's easy bucket on this theme holds TWO words, the search board draws four to six words a board and repeats an already-served one by the third themed date, and the crossword's solver cannot build a single board from a set this thin (four of 28 easy rows, none of the 14 medium, none of 60 hard tried).

changelog.change: Registered the crossword generator: three interlocking masks, one per band, and gave a difficulty band a grid.
changelog.why: Row 21 - the fifth Game, and the first whose answers constrain each other. The grid is the difficulty dial and it is a band's own field, because how many answers a board asks for and how much of each one the crossings give away is exactly what a band is allowed to change. Two measurements shaped every mask here. FIRST, a Tamil grid can be interlocked but not fully checked: over the served set a single pinned position leaves a median of 103 to 556 candidate words and two leave 3 to 11, but THREE leave a median of one, so a 3x3 full word square fills 12 times out of 12, a 4x4 twice, and a 5x5, a 6x6 and a 5x5 with blocked corners never once. Every mask here is therefore a British-style lattice with unchecked cells. SECOND, and this is the one that decided the layout: 24.1 percent of served words open with an INDEPENDENT VOWEL and essentially none carries one anywhere else - 0.0 to 0.1 percent at every other offset - so a word beginning with a vowel letter cannot be crossed on its first letter, because no other word in the language can carry that letter at the position it would need. A lattice whose crossings land on other entries' first cells therefore refuses about a quarter of the vocabulary outright, and it measured 74.8 percent fills against 99.3 for the masks below, whose entries every one BEGIN on an unchecked cell. easy is 5x5 and asks four answers of five ezhuthu across four crossings, from the familiar half. medium is 6x6 and asks six answers of six ezhuthu across nine crossings, from the familiar half - the biggest board, and the best crossed. hard is 6x5 and asks five answers of five and six ezhuthu across six crossings, from anywhere including the rarest quarter: fewer crossings is less help, and its vocabulary is the whole set. The three length ranges do not overlap, so every servable row is claimed by exactly one band. gridRows and gridCols stay 8 and are read here as the CEILING every mask must fit inside, which keeps the phone-screen number in one place. attempts is 1 and UNREAD: writing a wrong letter into a square costs nothing on paper and should not here. hints is empty and that is a ruling - a crossword already prints a meaning per entry, free, before the player has written anything, so every rung the shared ladder can render is either that same fact or a fact about one of six answers, which makes its worth depend on whether that answer is still open. The help this Game gives instead is a per-entry reveal priced in the answer it hands over.

changelog.change: Registered the word-search generator: an 8x8 grid, four to six hidden words by band, no attempt limit and no hint ladder; gave a Game a gridRows and gridCols and a difficulty band a targets count.
changelog.why: Row 20 - the fourth Game, and the first whose board holds more than one answer. The grid is 8x8 and the 8 is a phone measurement rather than a preference: a cell has to hold the widest ezhuthu legibly, which is 36px, and eight of those with a 4px gutter is 316px against the 328px a 360px phone leaves after its margins - a ninth column is 356px and does not fit. The row count follows the column count because a square is the only shape whose diagonals are as long as its sides, and a diagonal shorter than a row would make two of the eight directions second-class. targets is the difficulty dial and length deliberately is not, which inverts what length does everywhere else in this repo: a longer word covers more cells and is more distinctive, so it is EASIER to spot, while a four-ezhuthu word hides in the filler. All three bands therefore span 4 to 6 ezhuthu and separate on how many words are hidden and how well the player knows them - 4 words from the most familiar quarter, 5 from the top half, 6 from anywhere. Six is the ceiling because placement was measured: an 8x8 grid takes four, five, six and seven words on every one of 200 draws and eight words on 88.5 percent of them, so seven is the last count that never fails and six leaves a margin. attempts is 1 and is UNREAD - a wrong trace on a word search costs nothing anywhere in the world and should not here, because tracing IS how a player looks and charging for looking would turn the one exploratory mechanic in the game into a guessing game. hints is empty and that is a ruling rather than an omission: this board prints the words it is asking for, so category, first-ezhuthu and meaning are all facts already on the screen, and the one thing a player lacks - a location - cannot be a baked rung, because its text has to name one particular word and would be worth nothing if that word were already found. The help this Game gives instead is a reveal priced in the word it hands over, which lives in the Game because its cost depends on what is still unfound.

changelog.change: Registered the wordle generator: 6-ezhuthu answers, 8 attempts, three bands separated on familiarity alone, and a two-rung ladder.
changelog.why: Row 19 - the third Game, and the first whose knobs were set by simulating the game rather than by porting a convention. attempts is 8 and it is the load-bearing number. Modelled against a player who guesses a familiar word still consistent with every mark so far, a 6-ezhuthu board is solved within 8 guesses 94.5 percent of the time on the easy band, 93.5 on medium and 85.5 on hard - against 86.2 / 84.5 / 71.5 at seven. Seven is the N+1 the English wordles use and it would lose better than one hard day in four, and a hard day is one slot of every three. Tamil earns the extra row honestly: its alphabet is 247 ezhuthu against English's 26, 203 of them are in play in this set, and the best fixed opening word among 400 candidates averages 1.13 marks a game where a good English opener averages about two. Narrowing the hard band to drop the rarest quarter was measured as the alternative and REJECTED: q3 alone solves 75.0 percent within 7 and q4 alone 74.0, so the quarter costs a quarter of the vocabulary and buys one point - once the length is pinned, what decides whether a board is winnable is information per guess, not how rare the answer is. The bands are therefore all 6 to 6 and separate on maxStratum alone, which is the honest shape once the width is fixed: with one width the only thing left that makes a word hard is how well the player knows it, and the set splits 1,540 / 1,540 / 3,080 across the bands so every one of them fills. reveal stays 0 - handing over the first ezhuthu would be the strongest hint in the game given away for nothing, and this ladder deliberately refuses to sell even that. The ladder is two rungs: firstEzhuthu is refused because the player can buy the same fact by spending a guess, and one guess answers five other positions at the same time, so the rung is strictly worse than the move it competes with. choiceCount is untouched and unread - there is no bank in this Game; the keyboard is a composer over the 247-ezhuthu inventory, which is a fact about Tamil rather than a per-puzzle knob. categoryLabels is restated rather than shared because hint wording is per-Game by contract.

changelog.change: Registered the missing-letters generator, and gave a difficulty band a blanks count and a Game a choiceCount.
changelog.why: Row 18 - the second Game, and the first proof that adding one is a registry entry plus a payload builder rather than a rewrite of the day loop. Both new knobs carry defaults that leave every day baked before them valid and the anagram's entry untouched. blanks sits on the BAND because hiding a second ezhuthu is a difficulty dial and the bands are where difficulty is declared; it is the honest way to make a band harder, since it multiplies the guess space instead of reaching for a rarer word, and the contract refuses a band that could hide every ezhuthu of its shortest word. It is 2 only on hard, and hard starts at five ezhuthu, because measured over the 25,210-row served set a two-blank mask has a single answer for 96.7 percent of five-ezhuthu words and 100 percent of six, against 42.0 percent at four. choiceCount is a real balance number rather than a layout preference: there is no Tamil keyboard in this game, so the bank is how a hidden ezhuthu is entered at all, and its size is the odds a player who knows nothing still guesses right inside the allowed attempts - 8 puts that at 3 in 8 for a one-blank puzzle and 3 in 56 for a two-blank one. The ladder is two rungs, not three: firstEzhuthu cannot be sold here because this board has already printed every ezhuthu it is not hiding, so the rung is either a fact on the screen or the answer itself. categoryLabels is restated rather than shared because hint wording is per-Game by contract - it lives beside the templates - and this Game's is identical today only because nothing has asked it to differ.

changelog.change: Rebuilt the hint ladder: deleted the length rung, added a category rung at cost 1 and a meaning rung at cost 3 either side of the existing first-ezhuthu rung at cost 2, and added categoryLabels holding the Tamil tag the category rung renders for each lexicon category slug.
changelog.why: Row 14 of the lexicon pipeline - the length rung charged one point for the tile count already on the player's screen, and offering it as one of two hints short-changed the player. The ladder is walked in order rather than chosen from, so its order is its pricing and the three rungs now escalate in what they return as well as in what they cost: a tag, then a letter, then a phrase. categoryLabels lives here rather than in copy.json because hint wording lives here - the Tamil templates already do - and the lexicon's categories column holds English slugs, since a category is a machine dimension there. A slug with no label has no rung: a ladder that is sometimes two rungs is correct.

changelog.change: Added themeEveryNDays and gave the anagram generator its first themed wordlist.
changelog.why: Row 15 of the lexicon pipeline - a themed set nothing draws from is a dataset nobody reads, so the day loop needs a place to find one. A theme is registered per Game beside its ordinary wordlist, and the day runs it only when a whole playlist can be drawn from it. themeEveryNDays is 7 because the theme is wide enough to fill months of consecutive days, and a Daily that is nature every day for a season is the opposite of the variety a theme exists to add; one themed day a week is also the cadence the theme's growth target was sized against.

changelog.change: Gave every difficulty band a maxStratum bound alongside its length bounds, and moved the length bounds to 3-4 easy, 4-5 medium, 5-6 hard.
changelog.why: Row 12 of the lexicon pipeline - difficulty is two-axis, because length alone is anti-correlated at both tails: a long Tamil headword is usually a compound that decomposes and is easier than its tile count suggests, while a short rare word is brutal. The old easy band was minLength 3 / maxLength 3, which forced the generator into the shortest words - disproportionately literary, and brute-forceable at six arrangements against three attempts. Bounding easy to the most familiar quarter is also what makes it impossible for a day to be three words nobody knows.

changelog.change: Initial daily-engine registry: the anagram generator, its difficulty bands, and its hint wording.
changelog.why: Row 13 - the daily puzzle engine is a separate layer from the corpus, so its knobs are a separate file from the runtime app config.
